points.t: A patient with a new melanoma diagnosis asking what their report, stage and treatment mean.
Breslow thickness and ulceration set the T category; nodes (N) and spread (M) set the stage.

Excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin; wide local excision (0.5/1/2 cm by stage, NG14 2022); consider SLNB above Breslow 0.8 mm with risk features; adjuvant immunotherapy or BRAF/MEK for resected stage III (and some IIB/IIC).
Quoting outdated survival data: AJCC 8 5-year melanoma-specific survival for stage IIA is about 93–94%, not 80%.

points: **Excision biopsy with a 2 mm clinical margin**, full thickness including subcutaneous fat, oriented to allow later WLE/SLNB (along the long axis of limbs).
Done by the skin cancer team/specialist. In primary care, **refer rather than excise** suspected melanoma (NICE IOG).
**Avoid shave, punch or incisional biopsy** except for specialist situations (large facial LM, acral/nail).
If N0 (clinically and after SLNB), this is **stage IIA**, with ~93–94% 5-year MSS. The course "~80%" reflects older AJCC 7-era data, and it is closer to stage IIC today.
**Mitoses >5/mm² do not alter the stage in AJCC 8** (they are prognostic only).
If SLNB is positive → stage III (e.g. T2b N1a = **IIIA**).
Until SLNB is done, the stage is clinical ("cIIA").
Gershenwald JE et al. Melanoma staging: evidence-based changes in the AJCC 8th edition. *CA Cancer J Clin* 2017;67:472–92.
Keung EZ, Gershenwald JE. AJCC 8 update. *Expert Rev Anticancer Ther* 2018.

items.t: New lumps in or near the scar, in the limb between the scar and nodes, or new nodes: **urgent** review for **recurrence or in-transit disease**.
Survival figures change with each AJCC edition: use AJCC 8 (Gershenwald 2017) when counselling.

pearls.t: Patients often confuse lesion size with thickness. Explain: "Breslow is how deep it went, measured under the microscope."
